quarterly_data.signal: FY2025 results (CFO Roger Dassen, results press conference): Q4 2025 was a record quarter in sales, order intake and cash flow generation (CEO: 'record quarter record year, record booking'; no separate Q4 figures were given on the call). FY2025 net revenue EUR 32.7 billion (a growth of 16% in '25), gross margin 52.8%, net income EUR 9.6 billion, EPS close to EUR 25. EUV was the main driver, growing 39% vs 2024 on more tools and significantly higher prices: most Low-NA tools sold in 2025 were 3800 tools, whose productivity rose from 160 wafers per hour to 220 wafers per hour with a commensurate price increase, plus revenue recognition of a number of EXE (High-NA) tools. Deep UV decreased 6%, mostly on lower China sales; installed base business grew 26% to EUR 8.2 billion on EUV service and upgrades. EUV plus immersion made up 90% of systems revenue; end use memory 34% / logic 66%. China was 33% of system sales and 29% of total sales. Shareholder returns: total 2025 dividend of EUR 7.50 proposed; EUR 7.6 billion of the EUR 12 billion buyback completed and a new EUR 12 billion program over a 3-year period announced.
quarterly_data.figure: net revenue EUR 32.7 billion; gross margin 52.8%; net income EUR 9.6 billion; EUV grew 39%; installed base EUR 8.2 billion (26% increase)

quarterly_data.signal: Outlook (CFO): Q1 2026 net revenue between EUR 8.2 billion and EUR 8.9 billion, gross margin between 51% and 53%, Installed Base Management sales 2.4 (up from 2.1 last quarter) on very high customer appetite for upgrades, since while new fabs are still under construction the fastest way to add capacity is to squeeze existing tools with upgrades. FY2026 net revenue EUR 34 billion to EUR 39 billion (a 12% increase at the midpoint 'with good potential as the bandwidth also suggests'), gross margin 51% to 53%, effective tax rate 17%. 'the real steam engine behind this growth is once again EUV': EUV business to go up significantly, installed base up, non-EUV about flattish (Deep UV up a bit for the big memory and advanced-logic customers, China down, metrology and inspection quite strong). China expected at approximately 20% of 2026 total sales (from 29%), still close to EUR 7.5 billion at the midpoint; the CFO called it a normalization after executing the backlog built while China was underserved during COVID, with China sales also declining in absolute numbers. Long term reaffirmed (CEO): 2030 revenue between EUR 44 billion and EUR 60 billion with a gross margin of 56% to 60%.
quarterly_data.figure: Q1 2026 net revenue EUR 8.2 billion to EUR 8.9 billion; FY2026 EUR 34 billion to EUR 39 billion (12% increase at the midpoint); gross margin 51% to 53%; China approximately 20%

quarterly_data.signal: Capacity and customer demand (CEO Christophe Fouquet / CFO): the last 3 months clarified the horizon for 2026 and most probably a bit beyond, as customers now believe in the sustainability of AI demand in memory and logic and are planning capacity: 'for a lot of our customers in 2026, capacity will mean market share'. Customer capacity announcements (TSMC, Samsung and Micron cited) now 'translate directly into need for more tools'. ASML expects more EUV shipments in 2026 even though 'we have increased the productivity of our tool by more than 40%'; EUV capacity added in recent years grew 'in average 25% year-on-year'. CFO: long-lead-time items (factory space etc.) are in place at ASML and in its supply chain, and ASML is raising its move rate every quarter because 'you cannot move from 44 units in 2025 to 80 units in 2026 doesn't work that way' (an illustration of why the ramp must be gradual, not a stated plan; unit type not stated), which will lead to 'a very, very meaningful increase in our capacity this year'. Asked about maxing out, the CFO said it will be a very busy year and an important factor is when customers have their fabs ready to receive the tools. Footprint: two major sites opened last year (Korea and the U.S.); groundbreaking of a second big campus (the Brainport Industries campus in Eindhoven) planned around May-June 2026, with people moving in as early as 2028; 2026 hiring continues in manufacturing and customer service.
quarterly_data.figure: tool productivity up more than 40%; EUV capacity additions in average 25% year-on-year

quarterly_data.signal: EUV roadmap: revenue was recognized on the first 5200B, the High-NA high-volume manufacturing tool, which was shipped, installed and accepted by a customer (unnamed) looking at putting it into high-volume manufacturing for its leading nodes. High-NA customers are still qualifying the tools with good results; 2026 is a year to prepare for insertion, with the first products manufactured using High NA in 2027, '28, and High NA enabling the shift to more advanced technology around '28-'29 for DRAM and logic. The vast share of 2026 EUV growth will be Low NA going into high-volume manufacturing. The number of EUV layers is increasing at key customers, raising litho intensity. R&D: the lion's share goes to EUV across 3 work streams (High NA, Low NA and the 'high productivity platform'); the high productivity platform is an EUV platform for early next decade that can take Low NA optics (more than 400 wafer per hour), High NA optics and potentially Hyper NA optics, letting ASML decide later when to introduce Hyper NA.
quarterly_data.figure: first 5200B revenue recognized; first High NA products 2027, '28; high productivity platform more than 400 wafer per hour early next decade

quarterly_data.signal: Non-EUV products (CEO): DUV immersion 2150 launched with sub-nanometer accuracy and more than 300 wafer per hour; the NXT:870B KrF system achieves more than 400 wafer per hour and is 'creating a lot of interest' because 'productivity, again, is capacity'. 3D integration: the first TWINSCAN XT:260 was shipped last quarter with a 'lot of interest from our customer', ASML's first product for this market, with more products to be defined with customers. Metrology and inspection grew by almost 30% in 2025 (the CFO cited a 20% increase in applications) on the need for more process control at leading nodes; multi-beam e-beam inspection is progressing toward high-volume manufacturing in the next couple of years.
quarterly_data.figure: 2150 immersion more than 300 wafer per hour; NXT:870B more than 400 wafer per hour; metrology and inspection growth almost 30% in 2025

quarterly_data.signal: Reorganization announced with the results: 1,700 people leaving the company, 1,600 from the technology organization plus 100 from IT. The technology organization has about 4,500 leaders and needs about 1,500 after simplifying processes (3,000 fewer leadership roles), of which 1,400 become new engineering positions; the aim is faster response, quality and new products after feedback from customers, engineers and suppliers, with the change mostly within D&E. Management said the move is not about saving money; restructuring costs 'would not be considered material', and timing depends on talks with the unions and works council ('a number of months').
quarterly_data.figure: 1,700 people leaving; about 4,500 leaders to about 1,500; 1,400 engineering positions

players.product: EUV lithography scanners (NXE/EXE) for sub-1y DRAM patterning

quarterly_data.signal: AI memory shortage (CEO Christophe Fouquet): 'it's difficult to say if logic or DRAM is the bottleneck for AI today. I will still pick mostly memory', because demand for high bandwidth memory (the AI memory) is extremely high and demand for DDR memory is also very high, so DRAM prices went up significantly in recent weeks. Memory customers are moving very aggressively because 'capacity is also market share'; 2026 memory demand 'will be very, very tight', and DRAM customers started building capacity as quickly as possible most probably at the end of last year. DRAM and logic customers are building mega fabs, some talking about a hyper-cycle; Micron has been announcing groundbreakings almost every week, a direct translation into ASML shipments. CFO: memory was 34% of 2025 system sales (logic 66%), slightly lower as a share, but 'We actually see that flip in 2026', with memory becoming more and more important. High NA is to enable DRAM's shift to more advanced technology around '28-'29.
quarterly_data.figure: memory 34% / logic 66% of 2025 system sales; memory share to flip higher in 2026

contracts.signal: CEO: customer capacity expansions now translate directly into ASML tool shipments: 'Micron has been announcing groundbreaking almost every week for the last few weeks. There, you have a direct translation basically into shipment for us.'

quarterly_data.signal: AI wafer intensity (CEO Christophe Fouquet), using NVIDIA as the example: today's NVIDIA system (transcribed as 'black wall system') needs 'about 2.5 wafers to create the product', while the 2027 NVIDIA product (transcribed as 'revenue product') will need 10 wafers, so 'NVIDIA will need 4x more wafer than today', driving capacity extensions. For the most advanced AI products the transistor requirement has grown '16x every 2 years' vs Moore's-law 2x; when scaling cannot fit enough transistors, 'the only option will be to make more wafers'. Advanced logic and advanced memory are to grow 'more than 20% year-on-year for the foreseeable future' vs the historical 'about 6%, 7% year-on-year', and rising EUV layer counts at key customers raise litho intensity.
quarterly_data.figure: about 2.5 wafers today to 10 wafers in 2027 (4x more wafer); advanced logic and memory more than 20% year-on-year
